title: Loan Accounting Rules for Applying Payments to Operating Lines of Credit
content:
A payment on any of the Operating Lines of Credit is applied only while the line is in active, suspended or matured status.

## Rules

1. **Line status.** A payment may be applied only while the line is in active, suspended or matured status. The status is read from the association's record of the line the payment is for, before the payment is applied.
2. **Designated remittance.** A remittance the member designates — a principal paydown, or payment of a named interest bill or fee — is applied as designated, up to what is owed on that item.
3. **Undesignated remittance.** An undesignated remittance is applied in the product's payment order: fees (oldest assessment first), then billed interest (oldest due date first), then principal. Interest accrued but not yet billed is not collected except at payoff.
4. **One entry per item.** Each application is booked as its own entry: one interest payment entry per bill paid, pointing to that bill, and one fee payment entry per assessment paid, pointing to that assessment, all with the remittance's effective date and channel.
5. **Prepayment.** Principal may be prepaid at any time without penalty. On a revolving product the repaid amount becomes available again; on a non-revolving product it does not.
6. **Excess.** A remittance larger than everything owed on the line, including the final accrual at payoff, is not accepted for the excess.

## Status table

| Line status | Payment applied |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Suspended | Yes |
| Matured | Yes |
| Applied, declined or closed | No |

## Case (hypothetical undesignated remittance)

A line owes a USD 30 fee assessed in March, a USD 50 fee assessed in May, an interest bill of USD 400 due 15 April and an interest bill of USD 420 due 15 July. An undesignated remittance of USD 600 applied fees first is booked as four entries: USD 30 to the March fee, USD 50 to the May fee, USD 400 to the April bill, USD 120 to the July bill, and nothing to principal; USD 300 of the July bill stays owed.

## Case (hypothetical prepayment)

A USD 20,000 principal paydown on a Revolving Operating Line restores USD 20,000 of available credit; the same paydown on a Seasonal Operating Loan, which does not revolve, restores none.
